title: codemother's learning lands in tables she owns, and the chart-named ones move there
intention: CodeMother's learning lands in leaf tables she owns, codemother_<machine>_nodes, held by the librarian's delegation (outline 4.3.1.6-4.3.1.7): every codemother call into the tree tool names owner 'codemother', and the nine chart_<machine>_nodes tables holding her learning today move to codemother_<machine>_nodes with nothing lost.
why: Measured 2026-11-05: eight codemother calls pass no owner to the tree tool (cairn/tools/tree, OWNER = 'chart' default at tree.py:61): machines/orient/orient.py:554, deposit.py:139, survey.py:372, constrain.py:874, triage.py:258, validate.py:314, hypothesize.py:264, decompose.py:323; seed_trees.py and watch.py already pass owner='codemother'. So CodeMother's learning indexes sit in leaf tables owned by 'chart': chart_<nexus>_nodes rows constrain 537, decompose 532, hypothesize 4220, orient 531, survey 538, triage 526, validate 547, verdict 6, codemother 16 (codemother_root_nodes 47 is already hers). They are leaf (index) tables over the librarian's one shared node list; the nodes themselves do not move. watch.py:80 counsels as owner='codemother' with the default nexus 'orient', so it reads codemother_orient_nodes, which does not exist; its except swallows that and tree_hits is always 0. Two scratch leftovers chart_orient_far_3806085_035424_nodes (1) and chart_orient_ma_3806085_035424_nodes (5) are out of scope. Akien 2026-11-05: 'yes, codemother's learning goes in its own tables. they're still co-owned by the librarian and all that. and codemother does 'own' the learning blocks of her machines or tools that have them. but just as ownership of a set of trees is delegated to devices, same with the device delegating ownerhip to it's machines, and the machines to tools if we ever built one that complex. so we should update those that you identified'.
traces_to: Law 6 (each holder owns its corpus, delegated through the owner's gate; outline 4.3.1.6-4.3.1.7), Law 5 (the table's name tells a cold reader its owner), RULE 1 (codemother's own code; tools used through their public interfaces).
how: Pass owner='codemother' (a module constant OWNER = 'codemother' where the module has none) at each of the eight call sites; update the ten codemother proofs so their scratch nexi and assertions use the same owner. New one-shot cairn/devices/codemother/migrate_learning_to_own_tables.py: for each nexus in (constrain, decompose, hypothesize, orient, survey, triage, validate, verdict, codemother), if chart_<n>_nodes exists, store.create_owned_table('codemother_<n>_nodes', 'codemother', trees' leaf columns), copy every row through store.read/store.write, compare node-id sets, and only on a match store.drop_table('chart_<n>_nodes', 'chart'); print one line per table; exit non-zero on any mismatch. Run it live once after the proof is green (tables are backed up first with pg_dump -t to ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/temp/), and record its output in the voyage.

clauses.claim: an AST census of every non-proof module under cairn/devices/codemother finds no call to deposit_learning, counsel, propose, nexus_table or scratch_nexus without owner='codemother'
with a scratch nexus, survey's deposit lands its leaf row in codemother_<scratch>_nodes and none in chart_<scratch>_nodes

the migration over a scratch chart_<x>_nodes leaf of N rows owned by 'chart' leaves codemother_<x>_nodes owned by 'codemother' with the same node-id set and drops chart_<x>_nodes; a second run changes nothing; a node-id mismatch drops nothing and exits non-zero

live, read-only, after the migration has run: for each of constrain, decompose, hypothesize, orient, survey, triage, validate, verdict, codemother, codemother_<n>_nodes exists, store.owner_of says 'codemother', its row count is at least the 2026-11-05 census (constrain 537, decompose 532, hypothesize 4220, orient 531, survey 538, triage 526, validate 547, verdict 6, codemother 16), and chart_<n>_nodes does not exist

watch's tree counsel (watch.py) walks a codemother-owned nexus and returns hits for a vector deposited there in a scratch run, instead of raising into its except (measured 2026-11-06: it passed query_text=, a TypeError the except swallowed, so tree_hits was always 0)
every proof under cairn/devices/codemother stays green

decisions.text: Red-first proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_learning_lands_in_its_own_tables.py, check()/FAILURES/main() shape, one tooth per falsifier clause, PROVES = {'2b3d842bc118': {'1':..,'6':..}} (tooth names written at build). Clauses 2, 3 and 5 run on scratch leaves (trees.scratch_leaf / store.scratch); clause 4 only reads the live registry and counts; clause 6 runs the component's proofs.

Pass owner='codemother' at orient.py:554, deposit.py:139, survey.py:372, constrain.py:874, triage.py:258, validate.py:314, hypothesize.py:264, decompose.py:323; update the ten codemother proofs to the same owner.

cairn/devices/codemother/migrate_learning_to_own_tables.py: for each nexus in (constrain, decompose, hypothesize, orient, survey, triage, validate, verdict, codemother), if chart_<n>_nodes exists, store.create_owned_table('codemother_<n>_nodes', 'codemother', trees' leaf columns), copy every row through store.read/store.write, compare node-id sets, and only on a match store.drop_table('chart_<n>_nodes', 'chart'); print one line per table; exit non-zero on any mismatch.

Run the proof red, build, run clauses 1-3, 5, 6 green; back up the nine chart tables with pg_dump -t into ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/temp/; run the migration live once and keep its output; run the whole proof twice serially green. Commit before the hollow reading; seal with bin/cairn test --seal <path>.

D5: watch.py's counsel call passes query_text=, which tree.counsel does not take: measured 2026-11-06, TypeError: counsel() got an unexpected keyword argument 'query_text', swallowed by its except, so tree_hits is always 0 and every activation escalates to hex. Add module constant WATCH_NEXUS = 'orient'; call tree_counsel(vector, nexus=WATCH_NEXUS, owner='codemother', k=5) and count and extract findings from got['above_floor'] (counsel returns a dict, not a list). test_watch.py's [] mock of counsel is out of bounds and stays; reported.
